title: Baptism, St. Louis Cathedral and early public schools
summary: His mother prevailed on baptism at the cathedral; he went to catechism classes and to St. Philip's and McDonough 15.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Now, were you, given your father's proclivity against the Catholic Church, were you baptized?
Yes, I was. Yes, I was. Oh, yeah. My mother prevailed on him. That had to be.

Yeah, he relented. He would just teed off because the guy was trying to tell him what he knew wasn't right. And he's one of those guys you don't tell him when he knows something's right, or really believes it's right. You don't tell him it's wrong. Anyway, it was a minor blip in his lifetime, really, as far as he was concerned.
So, he brought in a major grudge against the Catholic Church?
No, no. In fact, he was usually pretty nice to him. Anyway.
What church were you baptized at?
Oh, because you all, was that your family church when you were growing up? You lived in the quarter?
Yeah, well, St. Mary's normally would have been. That was the Italian church. Yeah, but for reasons I don't know, my mother went to St. Louis Cathedral as a church.
But did you go there as a kid growing up?

Yeah, that's the school, that's the church I went to. That's where I was baptized, confirmed, all those things. Studied, you know, catechism in the after-hours classes because I went to public schools. I went to, actually, I started in St. Philip's School, the original school that's on the site of McDonough 15 now. Uh-huh. And then we were moved. I was maybe just in the first grade or so. I don't remember the exact year. We were moved to McDonough 15, which then sat on the grounds that are now empty at Barracks and Dauphine. Right. It was a big, empty lot there. And we stayed there until they built the new McDonough 15 in the early 30s and then transferred to there. So I went to McDonough 15 when it opened up for the very first time.
